APL wiring per glomerulus: the connectome numbers the model uses

QuestionHow much APL wiring does each antennal-lobe glomerulus get in the calyx, measured per unit of its input to the KCs, and is that pattern the same in hemibrain and male CNS?
Inputs
  • All in with_outside_ROI_synapses/claws_v2m2/ (corrected calyx, new claws; Report 02):
  • PN_calyx_weights_APL_vs_KC.csv: per PN, its calyx synapses onto KCs and to and from APL (Report 01)
  • odor_weighted/KC_APL_synapses_on_claws_by_glomerulus.csv: KC↔APL synapses that sit on a claw, with the claw's glomerulus (Report 02)
  • hemibrain_KC_claws_derived.csv.gz, malecns_KC_claws_derived.csv.gz: the claws (Report 02)
  • KC_weights_APL_PN_per_KC.csv: per KC, its calyx APL synapses (Report 01)
  • For Section 5: the corrected-calyx PN ↔ KC and PN ↔ APL synapses of all four connectomes
Outputs
  • with_outside_ROI_synapses/claws_v2m2/odor_weighted/APL_wiring_by_glomerulus.csv (one row per dataset × glomerulus)
  • the weights pgp_gpg​, qgq_gqg​ and the bouton share fff used in Report 05
  • reports/data/r04v2_pg_per_calyx.csv, r04v2_PN_calyx_weights_per_side.csv (pgp_gpg​ per calyx, all connectomes)
Scripts
  • scripts/apl_block_model.py, section "1. APL wiring per glomerulus" (APL_VARIANT=claws_v2m2)
  • scripts/reports/r04_prep_v2.py (per-calyx counts)
  • scripts/reports/r04_glomerulus_wiring.py (this report)

Report 05 lets APL's inhibition differ between glomeruli in three of its versions (P, L and M). This report explains where those per-glomerulus numbers come from. The model uses only hemibrain and male CNS (Yang, 2026-10-21), with the corrected calyx and the new claws (Report 02). Section 5 adds the bouton weight for every calyx of all four connectomes, as Yang asked. In the male CNS the two calyces are pooled here, because the per-glomerulus numbers are computed per dataset.

1The units: PN boutons, claws and microglomeruli

In the calyx, each PN axon forms boutons: swellings that carry its output synapses. Several KC dendritic claws wrap around one bouton, and the bouton with its claws is called a microglomerulus. APL makes synapses in both directions with both partners: APL→PN and PN→APL on the boutons, and APL→KC and KC→APL on the claws (Figure 1). Report 02 explains how they are found. Boutons are clusters of a PN's calyx T-bars within 2 µm. Claws follow Yang's corrected rule: a KC's calyx synapse sites are clustered at 8 µm along the KC skeleton, and each cluster is split by presynaptic PN (each PN with ≥ 2 PSDs gets its own claw). A KC↔APL synapse counts as on a claw if it lies within 8 µm, along the KC, of a PN synapse of that claw. Every claw belongs to one glomerulus: that of its PN.

2Six per-glomerulus numbers

Raw synapse counts mostly reflect how big a glomerulus is: how many PNs it has and how many claws. To compare glomeruli, each count is divided by a measure of the glomerulus's input to the KCs. For glomerulus ggg:

pg=# APL→PN synapses on PN(g)ngPN→KC,pgin=# PN→APL synapses from PN(g)ngPN→KC(1)p_g = \frac{\#\,\mathrm{APL{\to}PN}\ \text{synapses on } \mathrm{PN}(g)}{n^{\mathrm{PN\to KC}}_g}, \qquad p^{\mathrm{in}}_g = \frac{\#\,\mathrm{PN{\to}APL}\ \text{synapses from } \mathrm{PN}(g)}{n^{\mathrm{PN\to KC}}_g} \tag{1}pg​=ngPN→KC​#APL→PN synapses on PN(g)​,pgin​=ngPN→KC​#PN→APL synapses from PN(g)​(1)
all synapses in the calyx; ngPN→KCn^{\mathrm{PN\to KC}}_gngPN→KC​ = PN→KC synapses of the same PNs
qg=# APL→KC on claws(g)ngclaw,qgin=# KC→APL on claws(g)ngclaw(2)q_g = \frac{\#\,\mathrm{APL{\to}KC}\ \text{on } \mathrm{claws}(g)}{n^{\mathrm{claw}}_g}, \qquad q^{\mathrm{in}}_g = \frac{\#\,\mathrm{KC{\to}APL}\ \text{on } \mathrm{claws}(g)}{n^{\mathrm{claw}}_g} \tag{2}qg​=ngclaw​#APL→KC on claws(g)​,qgin​=ngclaw​#KC→APL on claws(g)​(2)
ngclawn^{\mathrm{claw}}_gngclaw​ = PN synapses on those claws

Two more divide the claw counts by the number of claws instead (cgoutc^{\mathrm{out}}_gcgout​ and cginc^{\mathrm{in}}_gcgin​, APL→KC and KC→APL synapses per claw). The model uses only pgp_gpg​ (version P, and M) and qgq_gqg​ (version L). pgp_gpg​ measures how much APL inhibition a glomerulus's boutons receive for each synapse they pass on to KCs. qgq_gqg​ measures how much APL inhibition its claws receive for each PN synapse they get.

4How much of APL's calyx output goes to boutons

Versions M0 and M of Report 05 put only part of the inhibition on the boutons, the same share as APL's synapses:

5The bouton weight in every connectome, per calyx

Yang asked for pgp_gpg​ in each connectome, one row per calyx. pgp_gpg​ needs no claws, so it can be computed for all four connectomes. Each calyx is counted on its own: an APL↔PN synapse belongs to the calyx of its APL, and a PN→KC synapse to the calyx of the nearest APL calyx synapse (each APL covers only its own calyx). The counts of the two calyces add up exactly to the per-PN table PN_calyx_weights_APL_vs_KC.csv (corrected calyx). A few PN types reach both calyces (V_ilPN, VL1_ilPN, VP1d_il2PN and some multiglomerular types); their synapses are split between the calyces accordingly.

  • The pattern is shared across connectomes. Over the 48 glomeruli the calyces correlate at ρs\rho_sρs​ 0.51–0.79 between connectomes, and 0.87, 0.75, 0.55 between the two calyces of FlyWire, male CNS and BANC.
  • The level differs between calyces, even within one brain: APL→PN per 100 PN→KC synapses ranges 0.58–1.56 (Table 5, all glomeruli), and BANC has the fewest. The pattern across glomeruli, not the level, is what the model uses (pgp_gpg​ enters relative to its mean).
  • The glomeruli at the two ends are mostly the same as in Section 3 (Figure 3).
Caveats

Synapse counts stand in for synaptic strength. Nothing here measures how strong a single APL→PN or APL→KC synapse is.

The model numbers (Sections 2–4) pool the two male CNS calyces, because the per-glomerulus weights are computed per dataset.

Glomeruli missing from the response tables still have weights, but they carry no odor input in the model.
